subject.title: perf(dev): gateway:watch triggers full rebuild on every startup when working tree is dirty

question: Should dirty watched source trees continue to force a dev rebuild, or should they fall through to mtime freshness when the build stamp is current?
rationale: The requested behavior improves the dev loop, but current tests and the gateway-watch helper treat forced dirty rebuilds as intentional and the mtime fallback has a real stale-dirty-file tradeoff.

options.title: Adopt mtime fallthrough
options.body: Update run-node, tests, and the gateway-watch regression helper so dirty-but-not-newer trees skip rebuilds while HEAD/config/missing-output invalidation still rebuilds.

options.title: Keep forced dirty rebuilds
options.body: Treat the current behavior as the intended safety contract and close this issue plus the candidate PRs with that rationale.

options.title: Defer for watcher policy
options.body: Leave this open until a broader maintainer pass defines dev watcher freshness, force-build escape hatches, and CI harness expectations together.

recommendation.title: Adopt mtime fallthrough
recommendation.body: Update run-node, tests, and the gateway-watch regression helper so dirty-but-not-newer trees skip rebuilds while HEAD/config/missing-output invalidation still rebuilds.

likelyOwner.reason: This is the clearest available owner signal because the dirty-source-tree optimization and shortcut branch trace to that commit history.
